geometry.source: 55_bus_mechanical (PEEK_GAP_MM · BORE_DEPTH_MM · LINER_* — from the CEMs at runtime); the Zone-3 shank length is a placeholder (HW.8.9)

twisted_run.top_clamped: the whole run twists as bare wire — needs a capture that clamps the wire itself, not in the tree
twisted_run.liner_bonded: the liner bonded to the wire over the bore as a parallel PEEK tube — the stiff bound; the angle to yield is smaller

holder.tube_torque_not_survival: first yield of a free tube: the fit's own stress, +40 °C and creep each lower it
holder.capture_at_pad_plane: not designed — the order assumes a capture that seizes the liner's top end
holder.parallel_tie: ice or resin in the wet gap or channel can carry torque to the wire past the tube; not bounded in the tree
holder.source: PEEK yield lib SIGMA_YIELD_PEEK_PA; contact pressure, area and μ sweep — 55's cache interference_window; creep floor lib PEEK_RELAX_FLOOR

bark_end_factor.reading: free-interface slip at the sleeve's bark end ÷ the centroid figure: the sleeve follows its local wood (decay length ≪ its length), the Ti part turns as the gyroid's centroid (rigid) or its top end (fully compliant); the factors above are applied at the rigid-gyroid value

wind_bark_end.source: 77 anchor_torque_path.json wind_bracket (rotation × bark_end_peak_factor, rigid gyroid — the larger); torque on the liner_bonded stiff bound

control.route: torque from the series compliance at θ_y, then the bare wire's surface stress — an identity: it catches coding slips in the run lengths, not modelling errors

verdict: Over the 35 mm run between the weld root and the pad plane the wire stays elastic below 9.7–11.5° on Ta (the lowest) and below up to 69.2° on beta-Ti-13Nb-13Zr — a fraction of a turn — and getting there takes 33.8–107.7 N·mm at its top. The only in-tree holder of that top, the PEEK liner, first yields in torsion at 13.7–15.9 N·mm — below the wire on every alloy, and below its own grip on every swept μ at the nominal and the creep-relaxed fit (the grip is zero at the fit's floor, +40 °C, and slips at once). With the tree's holder an unbounded event slip therefore yields or slips the liner — the channel's insulation — or slips the capture; the wire yields only if another link carries its yield torque: a capture that clamps the wire, or a parallel tie of ice or resin in the wet gap or channel. The order holds for any wire yield above 162 MPa. The wind's rotation at the sleeve's bark end is at most 2.75 mrad (pond) — at least 62× below the lowest wire budget — and forces at most 0.55 N·mm through the wire, far below the tube's yield.
